 Shopee Money+ Adds 5% Bonus for Malaysian Users
 October 21, 2026 by Editorial ShopeePay is giving Malaysian Money+ users the chance to earn indicative returns of up to 5% per annum during its latest promotional campaign. The offer runs from 1 September until 30 November 2026 and applies to eligible Money+ balances of at least RM200. However, the headline 5% figure is not a guaranteed flat bonus, so users should understand how the promotion actually works.
 Money+ combines returns from an underlying Shariah-compliant money market fund with an additional promotional top-up from ShopeePay. For this campaign, ShopeePay provides an extra 2% p.a. bonus on eligible balances, while the remaining return comes from the performance of the underlying fund. Since investment returns can change, the combined return could ultimately be lower or higher than 5% p.a.

 What Is ShopeePay Money+?
 Money+ is an investment feature available through the Shopee and ShopeePay apps in Malaysia. Money placed into Money+ is invested in the Eastspring Investments Islamic E-Duit Fund, a Shariah-compliant money market fund managed by Eastspring Investments Berhad. iFAST Capital distributes the fund, while ShopeePay provides the platform customers use to access it.
 This distinction matters because Money+ is not the same as leaving cash in an ordinary e-wallet balance. Money placed in the feature is invested, not held as electronic money or a conventional bank deposit. Returns are therefore variable and are not guaranteed.
 Money+ is intended to provide a relatively convenient way for users to put idle cash to work without leaving the ShopeePay ecosystem. Returns are calculated regularly and reflected in the Money+ balance. Users can also view their top-ups, withdrawals, investment returns, and promotional bonuses through the app.
 The 5% Figure Needs Some Explanation
 ShopeePay describes the campaign as offering indicative returns of up to 5% p.a. That figure includes the underlying fund return plus a promotional 2% p.a. Bonus Top-up from ShopeePay. It is not simply an extra 5% payment added to your balance.
 For example, if the underlying fund delivers a return of 3% p.a., the additional 2% promotional top-up brings the combined figure to 5% p.a. If the fund return falls below 3%, however, ShopeePay does not increase its bonus to make up the difference. The promotional component remains at 2% p.a.
 The reverse can also happen. If the fund performs above 3% p.a., eligible users can still receive the additional 2% promotional bonus. This means the combined return is not technically capped at exactly 5% p.a.
 How the Shopee Money+ Bonus Works

 Eligibility Qualified Malaysian Money+ users 
 The RM10,000 campaign balance limit is particularly important. ShopeePay only applies the 2% promotional top-up to the first RM10,000 held in Money+. Money above that amount can still receive whatever return the underlying fund generates, but it will not receive the campaign bonus.
 Users also need at least RM200 in Money+ to qualify for the promotional top-up. If the balance drops below that level on a given day, the bonus doesn’t apply for that day. This makes maintaining the minimum balance an important part of the promotion.

 How Much Could You Actually Earn?
 ShopeePay calculates the 2% promotional top-up using the eligible daily Money+ balance. ShopeePay calculates this portion by multiplying the eligible balance by 2% and dividing the result by 365 days. The underlying fund return is calculated separately and added alongside it.
 A RM10,000 eligible balance would generate roughly RM0.54 per day from the 2% promotional component alone. If the fund returned an equivalent 3% p.a., its portion would be around RM0.82 per day in this simplified example. Together, that would be about RM1.36 per day before accounting for rounding and changes in the fund’s actual performance.
 Smaller balances naturally generate smaller amounts. A RM1,000 balance receiving an effective combined 5% annualised return would work out to roughly RM0.14 per day on average. The promotion therefore provides a modest cash-management benefit rather than a large short-term payout.
 You Need at Least RM200
 ShopeePay requires participants to maintain at least RM200 in Money+ to receive the promotional bonus. A user holding RM199 would not qualify for the 2% Bonus Top Up for that day. Reaching or exceeding RM200 makes you eligible, provided you also meet the other campaign requirements.
 That threshold makes the campaign accessible to people who do not want to commit thousands of ringgit. You don’t need to deposit the maximum RM10,000 into Money+ to participate. The bonus simply scales with the amount you keep there.
 The RM10,000 figure is a cap, not a requirement. Someone keeping RM20,000 in Money+ would only receive the promotional 2% p.a. on the first RM10,000. The remaining balance would still be exposed to the underlying fund’s actual return.
 Returns Are Reflected Regularly
 Money+ returns are reflected in the user’s account based on when a top-up is made. Top-ups completed before the cut-off on a business day can generally begin reflecting returns that same business day. Later transactions may not be reflected until the following business day.
 Weekends and non-business days are handled differently. Returns and bonus amounts that fall over those periods can accumulate before appearing on the next business day. Users should therefore not assume that their balance will visibly increase every calendar day.
 Money+ includes a transaction history so users can see what is happening. The Balance Details section separates ordinary transactions from returns. This makes it easier to distinguish investment performance from ShopeePay’s promotional bonus.
 The Underlying Fund Is Shariah-Compliant
 Money placed into Money+ is invested in the Eastspring Investments Islamic E-Duit Fund. Eastspring Investments Berhad manages this Shariah-compliant money market fund. Eastspring is regulated in Malaysia, while iFAST Capital distributes the investment through the Money+ arrangement.
 Money market funds typically invest in short-term, liquid instruments. They are generally positioned as lower-risk investments compared with equity funds, although lower risk does not mean no risk. Returns can still fluctuate, and capital is not guaranteed.
 The Shariah-compliant structure could make Money+ relevant to a wider group of Malaysian consumers. Users looking specifically for an Islamic cash-management option may find that aspect particularly useful. They should still review the fund information before deciding whether it suits their needs.
 Money+ Is Not a Bank Savings Account
 Money+ can feel like a savings account because of its convenience, but legally and financially it is different. Your Money+ balance represents an investment in a fund, not money deposited with a bank. That distinction affects both risk and protection.
 Money+ balances are not protected by Perbadanan Insurans Deposit Malaysia. PIDM protection generally applies to eligible deposits held with member banks, subject to its rules and limits. Money+ does not fall into that category.
 Capital is also not guaranteed. Although money market funds are generally designed around relatively conservative investments, losses remain possible. Users should not treat the advertised return as risk-free interest.
 Why ShopeePay Is Offering the Extra 2%
 The promotional bonus gives ShopeePay a straightforward way to make Money+ more attractive. A potential combined return approaching 5% p.a. is more eye-catching than the underlying fund return alone. It may encourage existing ShopeePay users to try the investment feature.
 It also offers a broader ecosystem advantage. Money kept inside Money+ remains closely connected to the Shopee and ShopeePay environment. That gives Shopee another reason for users to stay within its financial services ecosystem rather than transferring spare funds elsewhere.
 The campaign also competes with an increasingly crowded Malaysian cash-management market. Banks, digital banks, e-wallets, and investment platforms now offer numerous ways to earn returns on spare cash. Promotional rates have become an important tool for attracting those balances.
 There Is a Campaign Budget
 One detail users should not overlook is that the promotional bonus is subject to availability. ShopeePay says the Bonus Top Up is available on a first-come, first-served basis until the allocated campaign budget is used. That means eligibility conditions alone do not necessarily guarantee that the promotion will remain available indefinitely.
 This matters because the campaign is scheduled to run until 30 November 2026. The stated end date does not necessarily mean promotional funds cannot be exhausted earlier. Users joining late should check the current campaign status inside the app.
 The underlying fund remains separate from this promotional budget. If the bonus allocation runs out, Money+ does not automatically stop functioning. It would simply affect the additional ShopeePay-funded portion of the return.
 How the Bonus Compares With the Fund Return
 The campaign essentially gives Money+ users two separate sources of return. One comes from the Eastspring fund and moves according to the fund’s performance. The other is the fixed promotional 2% p.a. top-up provided by ShopeePay on qualifying balances.
 That distinction explains why Shopee describes the overall rate as indicative. ShopeePay controls the promotional component but does not guarantee what the fund will earn. The final combined result therefore varies with the underlying investment.
 It also means users should not focus solely on the 5% headline. Understanding the underlying fund remains important because that is where most of the investment structure sits. The campaign bonus is temporary, while the fund itself continues beyond the promotion.

 What Happens After 30 November?
 The current bonus campaign runs until 30 November 2026 at 11:59 pm Malaysian time. Unless ShopeePay extends or replaces it, the extra promotional 2% p.a. ends when the campaign ends. Users would then continue receiving the actual investment return generated by the Money+ fund.
 This is another reason not to treat 5% as a permanent Money+ rate. Promotional returns can change whenever ShopeePay launches a new campaign. Long-term expectations should therefore be based on the underlying fund rather than temporary incentives.
 Is Shopee Money+ Worth Using?
 Money+ could be useful for people who already use ShopeePay and want a convenient place to keep spare cash. The RM200 minimum for the promotional bonus is relatively accessible, while the RM10,000 ceiling gives users room to earn the extra return on a larger balance. Having returns reflected directly within the app also makes the process straightforward.
 The biggest attraction during the campaign is clearly the additional 2% p.a. bonus. Combined with the fund’s return, ShopeePay is advertising indicative returns of up to 5% p.a. That can be competitive for money that might otherwise sit idle.
 The trade-off is investment risk. Money+ is not a guaranteed savings account, and the balance is not protected by PIDM . Anyone considering it should weigh the potential return against those differences.
